question.en: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme is a paradigm shift in India's industrial policy. Discuss its significance in achieving the goal of an Atmanirbhar Bharat.

introduction.en: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, introduced to boost domestic manufacturing, marks a shift from input-based subsidies to performance-linked incentives. It is a cornerstone of the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative.
introduction.hi: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, introduced to boost domestic manufacturing, marks a shift from input-based subsidies to performance-linked incentives. It is a cornerstone of the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative.

body.en: The scheme addresses the 'cost disability' faced by Indian manufacturers due to infrastructure gaps and high logistics costs. By providing incentives on incremental sales, it encourages firms to scale up production, achieve economies of scale, and become globally competitive. It specifically targets sectors like electronics, pharmaceuticals, and automobiles to reduce import dependency and integrate India into global value chains.

conclusion.en: While PLI provides the necessary financial push, its long-term success depends on complementary reforms in land, labor, and logistics to improve the overall ease of doing business.
